Latest Update: Welcome to the Repair Café, Where Neighbors Fight Throwaway Culture

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This story originally appeared on Grist and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
  • Sources indicate that on an unusually cool and rainy Saturday morning in Decatur, Georgia, dozens of people filed into a warehouse at the back of a church parking lot, their arms full of what a less hopeful group might call junk.
  • That’s how Lilly Pettus ended up shoulder to shoulder with three strangers, their hands all pressing together the pieces of her family’s cracked dining room chair as wood glue hardened and a volunteer tightened a clamp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This story originally appeared on Grist and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

Sources indicate that on an unusually cool and rainy Saturday morning in Decatur, Georgia, dozens of people filed into a warehouse at the back of a church parking lot, their arms full of what a less hopeful group might call junk. Some carried broken lamps, glitching electronics, or cracked furniture. Others walked in with toolboxes, multimeters for testing electric currents, and cans of WD-40. Beneath extension cords dangling from the rafters, they sorted themselves into smaller groups: the volunteer electricians, tailors, luthiers, carpenters, and at least one cutler (knife sharpener), commandeering nearby worktables and passersby as needed.

That’s how Lilly Pettus ended up shoulder to shoulder with three strangers, their hands all pressing together the pieces of her family’s cracked dining room chair as wood glue hardened and a volunteer tightened a clamp.

It has been revealed that “This is so interesting,” a giddy Pettus said, inspecting for the first time the joints, one of them broken, that held together the chair she’d owned for decades. “You never even know how furniture is put together.”.

Industry observers note that this is Decatur’s semi-regular repair café, one of a few hundred meetings like it across the United States. More Americans than ever are turning to these community gatherings to fix what they already own, resisting the influence of companies that sell everything from hiking boots to smartphones and hot water boilers and that push for replacement over repair. One consequence of this throwaway economy is an increase in greenhouse gas emissions from manufacturing that threatens to intensify climate change.

Recent findings suggest that yet, organizers and volunteers consider repair cafés to be more than a relatively small climate solution. As inflation rises and wages stagnate, the meetups connect people to a movement with the ambitious goal of changing the fundamentals of America’s consumer economy.

At the Decatur repair café, volunteers, wearing green shirts with “I can probably fix that” printed on the back, offered their skills free of charge as patrons observed. A young father of a toddler and squirmy baby watched as a volunteer replaced a switch on a favorite mid-century modern lamp worn out by the older child’s repeated clicking. Murmurs of excitement rippled around the building as the acrid smell of a spot welding project wafted through.

Pettus’ broken chair held in its wood her family’s story. Soon after she and her husband were married in 1996, they began a search for a dining room set. Pettus wanted the chairs to be comfortable for her entire family, but one of her brothers is nearly 7 feet tall, and another just a few inches shorter. “We are not a tiny family,” Pettus noted. “We are a substantial family.”.

Pettus also thought of one of her children who’d interned at the Environmental Protection Agency and shared his concerns with Pettus about pollution and climate change. Then, after months of the broken chair cluttering the family’s house, Pettus was running Saturday morning errands when she passed the Decatur repair café. She drove the half-mile home to grab the chair and decided to give it a second chance.

“When a product breaks and you have to throw it away, it’s very lonely,” said Martine Postma, director of Repair Café International, a Netherlands-based network of 4,000 cafés. “ It’s easier to just go on the internet and order a upcoming item which will come to your doorstep in 24 hours, but that’s also a very lonely, disconnected activity.”.

Postma, a former journalist with the demeanor of an unflappable librarian, founded her organization in 2010 after the birth of her second child magnified her fears about the planet’s future. “Markets are flooded with trash—with cheap products that we don’t need and that do not work,” Postma remarked. “They break, and they contribute nothing to our well-being. They just contribute waste.”.

Repair cafés appear to be inspiring people to use their stuff longer. In 2025, they prevented nearly 2 million pounds of waste—the equivalent of more than 100 fully loaded Boeing 747 aircraft—according to Repair Café International, and reduced greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to the average consumption of about 1,000 Dutch families.

It has been revealed that postma, Pettus, and millions of others often smack into obstacles when they try to fix their own stuff. Broken products are increasingly difficult to repair, according to a report from the Federal Trade Commission titled “Nixing the Fix.” The report details how Americans are incentivized to “replace products before the end of their useful lives” by companies that decide to make repairs less safe, limit the availability of parts, lock software and firmware, or even “disparage” independent repair.

In 2023, California, Colorado, Minnesota, and New York passed “right to repair” legislation meant to encourage repair over replacement. A year later the European Union passed a similar directive. Postma and other organizers consider the cafés a natural place for activism to push for right-to-repair measures, although Postma hopes for more sweeping changes in Europe, like a tax on raw materials. She argued it would limit emissions and bolster repair shops, even if it increases the cost of products.

“ I feel for the objects around me. I feel sorry for them if they’re broken,” she mentioned. “I want to make repairing a normal thing in everyday life once more.”.

According to Postma, repairing goods is more common in relatively poor countries where replacing them can be especially difficult and expensive. It’s in wealthy countries that repair cafés are thriving, but they’re not at all uniform. Each reflects the surrounding area and its socioeconomics.

On a Sunday afternoon in the Collier Heights neighborhood of Atlanta, volunteers brought most of their own tools to the basement of a building owned by a Seventh-Day Adventist Church, setting them on white plastic folding tables atop a light pink carpet. The café looked much different from the one a 30-minute drive across the city in Decatur. The median annual household income in the mostly Black Collier Heights neighborhood is roughly $40,000 lower than in Decatur. Many people who brought items wanted them fixed less for sentimental reason, and more so they could keep using them.

Industry observers note that gale Pines walked in with a red air fryer that had stopped working after they used it to dehydrate ginger. When their oven ran, Pines noted, it heated the entire kitchen. So, while in nursing school, they cooked many of their evening meals in the air fryer, most often chicken nuggets and fries.

Pines recently graduated but had trouble finding a job and couldn’t afford to buy a new $100 air fryer. “It’s just hard to exist,” Pines noted. “I don’t really have a very major support network outside of my friends.”.

One of Pines’ housemates told them about Collier Heights’ repair café. They keep a bag of broken electronics in the garage that they’d prefer not to send to a landfill. “Being in the height of climate collapse we can’t just keep buying fresh stuff all the time, both for the economy and for our material scarcity,” Pines noted.

When a volunteer at the Collier Heights repair café opened up the air fryer, they promptly discovered the problem: a bad capacitor. Another volunteer had brought a replacement part, and the two of them made the fix as Pines watched, impressed, but unable to follow the relatively complex repair. Pines felt OK that they hadn’t learned how to fix the air fryer themself.

“ To just be around people that want to help other people with the skills that they have, that’s value that is really key to me and something that I try to do as well,” Pines mentioned. “If somebody in my community has a question about their medication or something and can’t afford to go to the doctor, I’m happy to answer any questions that people have.”.

Another volunteer, Lew Lefton, noted he thought that the satisfaction humans draw from making and fixing things has largely been lost, but apocalyptic threats like climate change and artificial intelligence have driven many people toward rediscovering more basic, human skills that are key to survival. People who come to a repair café have a different way to view the future, according to Lefton, especially if they learn something or volunteer themselves. “If the world ends,” he said, “at least I’ll know how to fix a motor.”.

Recent findings suggest that back in Decatur, Pettus left the repair café with a newly sturdy chair. A screw and some glue fixed the crack around the joint, but the chair still needed upholstery work. Someone Pettus met at the café, who had provided one of the sets of hands that held her chair together as the glue set, advised her on where to buy fabric. Pettus thought she might bring the chair back to the repair café for help reupholstering its seat cushion.

Recent findings suggest that “The beauty of it,” Pettus remarked, “was that I actually was able to learn more about the chair. It was a great experience to know that—I’m not gonna say I birthed it, I of course did not—but I actually had something to do with helping to get it put back together.”.

I have to be honest here: most streaming deals aren't going to turn your finances around in any life-changing way. The Black Friday streaming price cuts have become steadily less tempting over the past few years. They're just not as impressive as they used to be. It's also worth noting that most deals apply only to the ad-supported tiers (with just a few exceptions). Still, any and every discount is welcome in a time when prices keep rising. Every cent counts, and it's easy to lose track of just how much you spend on streaming — especially if you're signed up for more than one service.

In a recent development, most streamers revealed their Black Friday deals early this week, but you may be wondering if there are still more to come. With just a few days until Cyber Monday, I'd say the best streaming deals have already arrived. I can't imagine that many more will pop up at this stage.

It has been revealed that I'm shocked that Peacock's Black Friday deal is as good as it is for 2026. Last year, the streamer didn't offer a deal at all, so this is light-years better than I was expecting. If you've been holding off on subscribing, now is likely the only time you'll get a decent discount. The Paramount+, HBO Max, and Disney+/Hulu Black Friday offers are pretty much on par with their deals of years past. I would lock in HBO Max and the Disney+/Hulu bundle for a full year, as more price increases could pop up in 2027. Paramount+ tends to offer discounts throughout the year more than any other streamer, so if you miss out on this one, it's no biggie.

According to recent reports, it's not worth holding on for a Netflix Black Friday deal, unfortunately. Netflix has never offered a Black Friday discount, or any kind of discount for that matter. Netflix is the top name in streaming and obviously feels that it doesn't need to offer Black Friday deals. I don't expect this year to be any different, but I'm always willing to be proven wrong. It would be a nice and welcome surprise.

We'll be updating this list of the best Black Friday streaming deals on the off chance any more turn up, so be sure to check back for updates.

Scam Roblox cheat codes are injecting malware into computers, reports reveal

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1003 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kids looking for an easy edge in Roblox may be giving scammers access to the whole family computer.
  • According to recent reports, A Cybernews investigation found that Roblox generated more than 22 million cheat-related searches from 2018 to 2026.
  • With some context, it's understandable why Roblox makes for an easy target.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kids looking for an easy edge in Roblox may be giving scammers access to the whole family computer.

According to recent reports, A Cybernews investigation found that Roblox generated more than 22 million cheat-related searches from 2018 to 2026. That's more than half of all the cheat searches across the 17 major games the outlet tracked. Security researchers working at Cybernews say scammers are using that demand to pass off malware as working cheats.

With some context, it's understandable why Roblox makes for an easy target. The platform is free to download, but many of the games inside it put weapons, VIP perks, and rare items behind paywalls. Those usually cost between $5 and $50, according to Cybernews. That has led to a steady stream of stories about kids running up charges on a parent's credit card, and the RobloxHelp subreddit is full of parents asking how to get their money back.

"Kids without access to credit cards look to cut corners on YouTube and Google search," Cybernews writes in its report.

No other game in Cybernews' study came close. Over the past 12 months, Roblox drew nearly 3.9 million cheat searches. Counter-Strike 2 came in second with about 533,000. Adjusted for player count, Roblox gets 482 cheat searches per 1,000 players, more than six times Minecraft's rate.

According to recent reports, many Roblox cheats rely on script executors — third-party programs that let players run their own code inside Roblox games. Antivirus software routinely flags these tools, so young players have gotten used to clicking past Windows Defender warnings, according to Cybernews. Many also hand full administrator access to unverified files they found through YouTube videos and Discord servers. Back in March, a threat actor listed 50 million allegedly stolen Roblox logins for sale. Cybernews indicates they were likely collected by password-stealing malware running on infected devices.

A few months later, in August, security firm Bitdefender uncovered a campaign spreading fake "undetected" versions of Xeno, a popular Roblox executor, Cybernews reported. The downloads came with real cheat scripts so they'd appear to work, but also contained malware. That malware could steal Roblox logins, saved browser passwords, and Discord accounts. It could also record keystrokes and even capture webcam footage.

Sources indicate that these kinds of scams are even riskier if Roblox is played on a shared computer. If a child uses the same computer their parents use, malware can steal a parent's saved banking logins, work email, and personal files, too.

Sources indicate that last year, Check Point Research found a similar scheme aimed at Minecraft players. Fake mods posing as the popular cheat tools Oringo and Taunahi were spread through malicious GitHub repositories. They infected more than 1,500 devices starting in March 2025, TechSpot reported. The malware went after browser passwords, crypto wallets, and Steam accounts.

Part of why these schemes work is that growing up online isn't the same as knowing how a computer works. Younger generations grew up on phones and apps that hide things like file permissions and security settings, so a warning on a desktop computer can be easy to dismiss. A 2023 Dell Technologies survey of more than 15,000 people ages 18 to 26 found that 44 percent were taught only very basic digital skills in school, and 12 percent got no digital skills education at all, according to Fortune.

The headphones are exceedingly comfortable and have excellent ANC—far better than basically every other set of headphones at this new low price of $200.

Did you hear the news? Sony made a version two of their cult-classic Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones. This is the first time they are on sale, and at $200, are one of the best deals this Black Friday. They have outstanding sound, great noise-canceling, a comfortable fit, and a convenient, folding design well-suited for travel.

The Nothing Headphone (1) are a home run in looks and sound, and they are at their lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday. They’re solid noise cancelers with a bold, transparent design on the ear cups that's somehow techy, retro, and futuristic-looking. Among their best features are the on-ear controls, namely the clicky wheel that adjusts volume and the flat rocker paddle that you can push back and forth to move to the previous track or skip ahead, respectively.

The budget Nothing Headphone (a) and premium Nothing Headphone (1) Pro are also on sale, but the Headphone (1) is the most appealing deal in my view.

But I am still seeing the blue colorway of these excellent headphones at the lowest price I've clocked for these older cans. When they debuted in 2022, they were our top pick for over-ear headphones. My top over-ear headphone pick, the best-in-class Sony WH-1000XM6, is at its lowest price ever this Black Friday. These headphones are amazing across the board, with their high comfort, superior sound quality, and great noise-canceling capability.

Recent findings suggest that this is the lowest price I’ve ever seen on one of my favorite pairs of wireless earbuds. The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro have one magic trick: call quality. To put it simply, I sound better talking on calls using these earbuds than any other I’ve tested, and it’s not a close competition. Beyond that, they’re solid all-rounders, with good noise-canceling, sound quality, and versatility.

Industry observers note that want workout earbuds that won't fall out? Get these Beats Powerbeats Pro 2. They're some of the more secure-fitting earbuds I've ever tested. Plus, they have great noise-canceling, transparency, and even built-in heart-rate sensors, so you can track your workout even if you left your fitness tracker at home.

Sources indicate that the Nothing Ear (3a) are one of our favorite pairs of earbuds under $100, and 30 percent off is the biggest discount I've ever seen for them so far. They have a semi-transparent design and bold colors that stand out from the crowd (particularly the yellow version). While the automated noise-canceling isn't the best, it's hard to fault them at this new low price.

My main gripe with the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) is price. At 45 percent off (their lowest price ever), that complaint vanishes, making this a top headphone deal to shop. The headphones are exceedingly comfortable and have excellent ANC—far better than basically every other set of headphones at this new low price of $200.

It has been revealed that did you hear the news? Sony made a version two of their cult-classic Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones. This is the first time they are on sale, and at $200, are one of the best deals this Black Friday. They have outstanding sound, great noise-canceling, a comfortable fit, and a convenient, folding design well-suited for travel.

Sources indicate that the Nothing Headphone (1) are a home run in looks and sound, and they are at their lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday. They’re solid noise cancelers with a bold, transparent design on the ear cups that's somehow techy, retro, and futuristic-looking. Among their best features are the on-ear controls, namely the clicky wheel that adjusts volume and the flat rocker paddle that you can push back and forth to move to the previous track or skip ahead, respectively.

The budget Nothing Headphone (a) and premium Nothing Headphone (1) Pro are also on sale, but the Headphone (1) is the most appealing deal in my view.

The more premium XM6 and the newly revived (and cheaper) XM4C have effectively replaced the Sony WH-1000XM5. But I am still seeing the blue colorway of these excellent headphones at the lowest price I've clocked for these older cans. When they debuted in 2022, they were our top pick for over-ear headphones. They remain excellent and far outperform other options at this limited price.

Industry observers note that sony recently launched the WH-CN730N to replace these headphones, hence the rock-bottom price of 50 percent off. While these headphones can't compete with most specs of more premium options on this list, they're ultra-lightweight at just 192 grams. That weight plus 35 hours of battery life with ANC on is nothing to scoff at.

AirPods Max 2 are excellent over-ear headphones for Apple fans, but the $550 sticker price is frankly absurd. Thankfully, they are almost always a little bit on sale, including now. This is far from the best deal I've seen on these headphones, and I do expect the price to dip further during Black Friday sales events, so I would add them to my cart and wait to pull the trigger.

According to recent reports, my top over-ear headphone pick, the best-in-class Sony WH-1000XM6, is at its lowest price ever this Black Friday. These headphones are amazing across the board, with their high comfort, superior sound quality, and great noise-canceling capability.

Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving Day is done. Finito. The turkey is eaten, the potatoes mashed, the football won (Editor's note: Go Bills!), and the Macy's parade, erm, postponed. All of which means Black Friday 2026 is officially here.

As Mashable's tech editor, I get to review some of the coolest gadgets in the world — and I genuinely love my job. The downside to covering tech in 2026? Having to constantly update Mashable readers on an endless stream of price hikes. Well, Black Friday is your chance to get some well-deserved relief for your wallet.

According to recent reports, the best Black Friday tech deals are counteracting many of the price hikes from the past 12 months, and in some cases, these deals go even further. I know a lot of people are wondering whether the discounts will be any good this year. Let me just say that so far, I've been pleasantly surprised. I've been covering Black Friday sales as a journalist since 2019, and this year, I've found discounts of 50% and up on flagship LG OLED TVs, noise-cancelling headphones from Bose, and upcoming Amazon Echo products.

Some of my favorite tech gadgets are also on sale. I'm talking about items I've personally tested and reviewed and now use all the time — in some cases every day — including the DJI Osmo Pocket 3, Apple MacBooks, Kindle Paperwhite e-readers, and the Sonos Arc Ultra soundbar. I also found discounts on trending products and holiday gift ideas, like the Kodak Charmera blind box (another personal favorite of mine).

Black Friday 2026 live blog: Top deals, store hours, and real-time updates.

In a recent development, remember: Most retailers' Black Friday sales have been running for over a week at this point, so the shopping is well underway. Be sure to grab the bargains before they get snapped up and disappear.

This year's Black Friday deals on Apple Watches are better than we expected. Case in point: You can pick up the Apple Watch SE 3 for just $179, its lowest-ever price, according to our research. The SE 3 came out in 2025, but it offers an always-on display and all-day battery life, meaning it's not too significant of a step down from the newly introduced Series 12, which is also at a record-low price, of course. A lot of people will be asking for these watches for Christmas, and this is your best chance to grab them on sale.

I don't think I've ever seen a 65-inch OLED TV for sale before — at least, not one that I'd recommend to Mashable readers. Now, to be clear, you are losing out on some of the brightness and other bells and whistles you'll get with the LG C6 or Samsung S90H, but you still get the famed OLED blacks and color clarity.

This year, we've gotten some actual Nintendo Switch Black Friday deals, which isn't always the case. Specifically, the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World Bundle is finally back in stock — and a little cheaper than usual — at Amazon, Best Buy, Target, and Walmart.

On top of that, Woot still hasn't sold out of its popular (and very rare) discount on the Nintendo Switch 2 gaming console. Since Woot deals tend to sell out quickly, hop on this one right now if you're interested. The $30 discount isn't much, but it leaves a little extra room in the budget for games like the upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Remember: Woot is owned by Amazon, so Prime members get free shipping.

Read our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2, which we recently named a Mashable Gift of the Year winner.

Recent findings suggest that the Mashable team has become obsessed with this little digital camera keychain. And we love it even more since it comes in a blind box. Recent findings suggest that bose has become a staple of Amazon's Black Friday sale. For comfort, audio, and noise cancellation, you can't beat the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen). We named them the most comfortable in our guide to the best earbuds.

According to recent reports, this Mashable-favorite just got a $70 price cut, which is good to see after it was hit by a price bump this year. I've been recommending this affordable and chic hand warmer in gift guides for the past five years, and so I couldn't resist including it as one of the year's best Black Friday tech deals (it does have a rechargeable battery, after all). You can even color-match this product to your latest burgundy or glacier blue iPhone 18 Pro.

In a recent development, I reviewed all of Apple's fancy new iPads for Mashable — the super-thin iPad Air, the iPad Pro with its incredible tandem OLED ProMotion display, and the brand-new iPad Mini OLED. If you're more likely to use your iPad to scroll Instagram, do some online shopping, and play The Sims — and who isn't? — then you'll be perfectly happy with the older (and more colorful) base Apple iPad, which is far more affordable.

If you want an even more affordable iPad, then I can happily recommend an alternative. Amazon recently ditched its Fire tablets for the latest line of Alexa tablets, and they're ready-made for casual scrolling and streaming, now with Android OS. Topics Apple Black Friday Bose MacBook Nintendo.

Industry observers note that this year, Black Friday falls on Friday, Nov. 27 (the day after Thanksgiving). However, the sales actually started a lot sooner. Amazon and Best Buy rolled out their official Black Friday 2026 sales on Nov. 19, Target began its savings event on Nov. 22, and Walmart kicked things off on Nov. 23.

Cyber Monday falls on Monday, Nov. 30 this year. While some stores will have a one-day-only sale on that date, most online retailers have evolved into offering a full "Cyber Week" sales event.

This year, you can find discounts of up to 50% or more on Bose QuietComfort Headphones, Hisense and LG TVs, and Amazon Echo smart home devices. You can also find significant discounts on virtually every Apple products, including record-low prices on the entire Apple Watch lineup, plus savings on MacBook and AirPods. For budget shoppers looking for the best tech deals under $50, we recommend checking out the JLab JBuds Lux ANC Headphones and Anker charging products.

Timothy Beck Werth is the Tech Editor at Mashable, where he leads coverage and assignments for the Tech and Shopping verticals. Tim has over 15 years of experience as a journalist and editor, and he has particular experience covering and testing consumer technology, smart home gadgets, and men’s grooming and style products. Previously, he was the Managing Editor and then Site Director of SPY.com, a men's product review and lifestyle website. As a writer for GQ, he covered everything from bull-riding competitions to the best Legos for adults, and he’s also contributed to publications such as The Daily Beast, Gear Patrol, and The Awl.

If you want a cheaper vacuum that still comes with two cleaner heads, the older Dyson V15 Detect is also already on sale ($599), and it's even bundled with the Car Cleaning Kit, meaning three extra attachments. The V15 was our top Dyson vacuum pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still packs two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). It's a great all-around vacuum, and this bundle option gets you great extra attachments.

Recent findings suggest that dyson had two different budget vacuums come out this year, but the V10 Konical was my favorite of the two. It has a modified version of the All Floor Cones cleaner head you'll find on the much more expensive V16 Piston Animal and did a great job in my tests; overall, it actually scored a little higher than the V15 Detect when tested side by side. It's often on sale for $400, but you can find it for an even better $350 right now during Black Friday.

Recent findings suggest that the PencilVac is incredibly handy and compact, and great if you're trying to do quick pickups daily on hard floors. You won't want it if you have any kind of rug or carpet, since it's only designed for hard flooring, but I did find it incredibly easy to grab and use for constant litter trails in my house. It's incredibly lightweight and a great fit for anyone with mobility or strength concerns. If these features speak to you, this is a great time to buy, as it's already on sale.

Sources indicate that this wet floor cleaner is often on sale for around $400, so it's not a huge surprise to see this deal ahead of Black Friday. The Dyson Clean+Wash is primarily a wet floor cleaner, but it can do dry cleans, too, and does not use a filter you inevitably need to keep clean. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck noticed no weird smells in three months of use. It's similar to the Dyson WashG1, with a self-propelled design that makes it easy to push around the room, and it does a good job scrubbing floors clean. Keep in mind that it's not great for dry debris, since it’s just rolling, not sucking.

It has been revealed that the Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai came out earlier this year and is one of my favorite robot vacuums from the brand. That's including the newer Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV I’m presently testing, which hasn't blown me away as a better investment. (It actually failed my corner test completely, which vacuums in that price range should not do.).

Recent findings suggest that the Spot+Scrub Ai is much lower priced, and despite some dubious AI feature claims, it does a good job cleaning autonomously. It’s often discounted around this price, but the $400-off sale is a little better than what I saw during Prime Day.

Be sure to see our guide to the Best Merino Wool T-shirts, Best Merino Wool Clothes, and the Best Base Layers for more great merino wool options.

What’s So Great About Merino Wool?

According to recent reports, merino wool is great because you're stealing a sheep's ability to keep itself warm or cool based on the temperatures it's in. This is a process often referred to as thermoregulation. Merino sheep have thinner, softer wool than what most people think of when they think of wool. The sheep evolved this soft coat to keep them comfortable across a wide range of temperatures. The result is a fabric that's comfortable to wear next to your skin. For the softest tees, look for fabrics that are either superfine or ultrafine—anything 17 µm or higher—like Unbound's T-shirts.

Industry observers note that wool is sustainable, too. One sheep can produce 4 to 5 pounds of wool per year. While cotton has its place, and so does the occasional synthetic garment, merino wool is a remarkable fabric that's the cornerstone of my wardrobe. I don't think you can have too many merino pieces in your closet, but they’re not cheap, which is why we're featuring these deals.

What’s So Great About Unbound Merino?

It has been revealed that I like Unbound's T-shirts because they're 100 percent merino wool, no synthetics involved. That means all the antibacterial, odor-resistant, moisture-wicking, temperature-regulating goodness of merino wool … just works. I've found Unbound's T-shirts in particular to be very quick-drying and wrinkle resistant, two of the reasons I think they're the best merino T-shirts for travel. The organization's pants also have a very high wool percentage (95 percent), and they roll up nicely, making them very packable. Do you need special travel clothing? No, but Unbound's merino wool is naturally odor-resistant, which means you need fewer pieces in your bag. The company also offers a 30-day guarantee. If you don't like it, you can send it back.

In a recent development, most merino products come with care instructions. Unbound Merino's T-shirts should be washed cold with like colors, then laid flat to dry. Whatever you do, don't bleach them and don't tumble dry them. The latter is especially destructive. I do it to every wool T-shirt I test, and it makes me sad, but I know some of you won't listen and will do it anyway, so I have to know what happens so I can warn you. Don't tumble dry. Just put it on a drying rack. It doesn't take more than a day. Seriously, you just spent $80 (on sale!) on a T-shirt; take care of it. Properly cared for, high-quality merino clothing like Unbound's is incredibly durable and will last for years. Throw it in the dryer and the pilling starts almost immediately.

Do I always lay them flat to dry? No. When traveling I usually hand-wash in the sink and then drape them over the shower curtain rod to dry, which hasn't seemed to have much negative impact. The challenges with hanging wool to dry is that it will stretch out from the water weight. This is particularly true with 100 percent merino, like Unbound's T-shirts.

In a recent development, I've never had a problem storing merino in my closet between wears, but for long-term storage, I recommend you take precautions against moths, which are notorious for eating holes in wool. I have lost merino garments to moths. I make sure to wash and thoroughly dry whatever I am storing, then I seal it in a compression bag. Another option is to put your merino garment in a cotton bag or otherwise wrap it in cotton and then put it in a plastic bin. It's very key to make sure that the garment is completely dry before using any of these storage methods; otherwise your wool will smell musty and moldy. Other options include storing your garment in a cedar chest, which is a good natural deterrent for moths, or use moth traps or lavender sachets, which will repel the moths.

Unbound Merino (Unbound Merino Women’s).

According to recent reports, unbound's T-shirts were my introduction to the brand, and they're still one of my favorite merino T-shirts. This T-shirt is incredibly soft, and because it's 100 percent merino wool, it'll stay odor-free for ages—as long as five or six days in my testing (depending on local temps, what you're doing, etc). Unbound's crew neck merino T-shirt has a relaxed, casual cut. It's not going for the technical look you'll get from many outdoor brands. It's also lightweight and packs down to a tiny ball, which is perfect if you're looking to simplify down to one bag. (Really, is there any other way to travel?).

The final thing I love about these is how fast they dry. In most climates, you can give it a wash in the sink at night, roll it up in a towel, wring it dry, lay it out flat, and it'll be dry by morning. If they have a downside, it's that Unbound's T-shirts do need to be babied a little. To help them last a long time I recommend hand washing and line-drying. Also note that while I like the merino crew neck, the V-neck is also on sale for $88 ($10 off).

Sources indicate that unbound's merino travel pants are a light and comfortable merino blend, with plenty of stretch and freedom of moment, thanks to the 5 percent elastane. These have a more formal look, what you might call slacks if you are a certain type of person. You might even be able to pull off going to office in them, but I'd sooner chew my leg off than work in an office, so I don't really know. I can say I've worn them to nice restaurants without a second look, and yet they don't scream “I've got money” when you're stumbling back to your hotel room in Prague at 4 am.

It has been revealed that as you would expect from anything Unbound makes, these pack down fantastically small. You can pack two pairs of these for every pair of jeans. Again, for serious travelers looking to live out of a single carry-on bag, that's huge. The only downside is that these are on the thin side, not something you'd want to wear alone in cold climates. If you're like me and have to deal with winter, throw a good base layer underneath them and you'll be fine. The slim fit pant is also on sale if that's more your style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You might have clocked it in the Season 4 premiere, but with episode 2 it's very clear: Molly Ringwald has joined Yellowjackets.

Industry observers note that the '80s icon who fronted movies like The Breakfast Club, Sixteen Candles, and Pretty in Pink takes over the role of Van's (Liv Hewson) mom, Vicky Palmer, from Deborah Vancelette. And this signifies a major change in Van's life, post-rescue.

According to recent reports, in the Season 1 pilot, Vicky (Vancelette) is presented as a bad mom. In a montage of the Yellowjackets readying for that fateful flight, Van walks through a dark, cluttered house to find her mom passed out on the couch, next to a nearly empty alcohol bottle. She tries to wake her, presumably because she needs a ride to the plane. But calling to her and shaking her isn't enough to rouse Vicky. So, Van slaps her, and she does so with a world-weariness that suggests this isn't an isolated incident.

In Season 4, episode 2, Vicky (Ringwald) is transformed. The living room is sunny and tidy upon Van's return, with a wall of VHS tapes carefully preserved. Later, Vicky indicates she cares by assuring Van she taped every episode of The X-Files. To Tai (Jasmin Savoy Brown), she'll say of Vicky, "My mom is completely different.".

In a recent development, no shade to Vancelette, who got little to do in the role of Vicky. But if any Yellowjacket was going to get a mom played by a movie idol of the '80s, it ought to be Van. Her love of pop culture is a defining characteristic, as she'd quote and allude to movies and reveals to brandish her wit and wisdom. Of course, if her mom's going to get a glow-up, she's going to become the "princess" from The Breakfast Club. This indicates that Van's mom knows she's up on her bills, and she knows her daughter.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re anything like me, you didn’t give your kids a phone or tablet the second they were out of the womb. Instead, I’ve slowly introduced them to personal devices as I felt it made sense, and a smartwatch was one of the first easy ways for them to stay in touch while away from home without being introduced to the dangers of the internet. This year’s Black Friday sales on Bark and Garmin kids’ smartwatches slash up to $64 off the regular price, making them an easier decision than ever to pick up.

According to recent reports, I’ve tested a lot of kids’ smartwatches over the years, and I can easily recommend the two in the picture above: the Bark Watch and the Garmin Bounce 2. Choosing between the two is easy enough. Garmin’s watch is simpler and comes in a slightly more durable case with fun colors. It’s slightly cheaper than Bark, but doesn’t have any health sensors on board. It mainly tracks steps, allows your kids to message or call you, and gives you geofencing and location tracking through a $9.99 per month LTE subscription plan. It’s got a 5ATM rating and a polycarbonate case, so it’s quite durable.

The Garmin Bounce 2 is preloaded with a few mini games and educational apps, plus the Garmin Jr. app has built-in unlockables and rewards parents can set for doing chores, completing schoolwork, etc. Battery life is roughly 2 days with normal use, but can be less if you’re in an area with poor LTE reception. The Garmin Bounce 2 is best for kids 10 and under.

According to recent reports, the Bark Watch uses Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 hardware and a custom version of Wear OS. It’s a much more powerful watch and only gets a day of battery life because of it. This one feels like a midpoint between a kids’ watch and a standard Wear OS watch, as it has all the power of Wear OS but doesn’t feature the Google Play Store. It doesn’t have any games, social media, or browsers.

Sources indicate that since it uses Samsung’s hardware, it includes cutting-edge health sensors that your kids can use, plus great multitasking and a svelte, attractive design. Bark charges $15 per month for its blueprint, which includes a Bark App subscription for the whole family. I also use the Bark App on my son’s phone, which helps me monitor his usage and make sure he’s safe online. The extra $5 per month adds up, but it’s absolutely worth it if you want to add the Bark App to another phone or tablet.

Industry observers note that the Bark Watch is fine enough for younger kids, but the design and lack of games feel more like an “older kids’ watch” to me, and my 12-year-old son agrees. Either way you go, these are fantastic choices that you’ll be happy with, especially with a nice little deal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The H3 Podcast has come to an end.

On Monday, Hila Klein declared on the show's Instagram account that she had "made the difficult decision to stop working on the latest show." She had been developing a crew-led version of the podcast since her estranged husband and co-host, Ethan Klein, was pushed out of it last month after she revealed his affair.

In a recent development, "I've come to realize that I can't continue down this path while also giving myself the space I need to heal and protect my mental health," she wrote. "Right now, I need to focus on myself, my healing, and what's best for me and my kids.".

Industry observers note that the announcement closes out a month-long fallout that began on Oct. 22. That day, Ethan said on Instagram Stories that the podcast was going on "indefinite hiatus." Hours later, Hila posted that he had been having an affair for more than six months. As Mashable previously reported, the crew said in a statement that they would not keep working with Ethan "involved or profiting in any way." Ethan said he was working to give up his financial stakes in the podcast and in the couple's businesses, including the clothing brand Teddy Fresh.

Recent findings suggest that complex reported that Hila filed for divorce on Nov. 2, listing their separation date as Oct. 13. The couple married in 2012 and share three children.

Since the news broke, multiple crew members have spoken out. On the show's Discord, longtime producer GirlWithAMicrophone (GWAM) mentioned she would not work on a project with the rest of the crew. She thanked Hila for giving them "a shot during all this turmoil.".

Producer AB Ayad suggested on X that the obstacles were bigger than any one person. "There are certain people involved that were never gonna allow us to continue doing the show together," he wrote, adding, "I give Hila a lot of credit that she was able to do what she even did.".

In a recent development, beyond the H3 Podcast, Ethan co-hosted Frenemies with Trisha Paytas, which became one of YouTube's most talked-about shows before it ended acrimoniously in 2021. He later started the political show Leftovers with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, which ended in 2023 over disagreements about Israel and the war in Gaza.

Since the announcement of the show ending, Ethan has broken his weeks-long silence. On Tuesday, in a series of Instagram Stories, he called the affair "the ultimate betrayal" to his wife and to the show's audience. He also remarked that "the show ending is entirely my fault.".

According to recent reports, however, he didn't rule out a comeback. "I will probably be back, but when and how, I can't tell you," he wrote, hinting at a solo show or a fresh project.

  • The final episode of Amelia Dimoldenberg's YouTube series is now live, and for her last date, she sat down with Belgian psychotherapist Esther Perel.
  • Recent findings suggest that the show's final guest, Perel, is best known for her work on relationships and intimacy.

After 12 years of awkward silences, flirting, and fried chicken, Chicken Shop Date is officially closed.

The final episode of Amelia Dimoldenberg's YouTube series is now live, and for her last date, she sat down with Belgian psychotherapist Esther Perel. Dimoldenberg, called by the BBC "one of the U.K.'s best-known content creators," declared in September that the show was ending.

Recent findings suggest that the show's final guest, Perel, is best known for her work on relationships and intimacy. So, given who's sitting across from her this episode, it's no surprise the conversation turns on Dimoldenberg and what it means to walk away from the show that made her.

"I can't stay here forever," Dimoldenberg states in tears near the end of the episode. "I need to leave the shop.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, well, it's finally here: Black Friday has begun. And no one does Black Friday harder than Amazon, which kicked off its savings a full week early. Now that the major day has arrived, you can save 50% and up on Amazon Echo devices. On top of that, Prime members who buy select Echo devices will also get a $40 free credit to spend on additional Amazon smart home products. And on top of that, we found tons more deals on Kindle e-readers, Blink cameras, and the brand-newly introduced Alexa tablets.

Sure, Black Friday technically falls on Nov. 27, but Amazon's official Black Friday Week started with a bang and is staying strong into Black Friday proper.

According to recent reports, if there's an Amazon device on your list, there are some massive discounts live on Fire TV Sticks, Kindles, Echo devices, and Alexa tablets. Since many of these devices saw price increases in 2026 (thanks, RAMageddon), this is your chance to cancel them out. But we're pleased to say that so far, many of these deals are surpassing expectations — particularly on the brand-new Echo devices.

Recent findings suggest that we'll be tracking all of the best Amazon device deals throughout Black Friday and Cyber Monday. For deals beyond Amazon devices, be sure to follow along with all of Mashable's coverage in our Black Friday hub.

Sources indicate that sadly, the entire Fire TV Stick lineup was hit with a price increase back in August. But that doesn't seem to affect how impressive the discounts are. Prime members can grab the brand-newly introduced Fire TV Stick 4K, which was released in September, for just $19.99. That's its best price so far on record.

Sources indicate that the 4K Select was only released last year, but the 4K has officially replaced it. It features the Vega 2.0 operating system for even speedier navigation and a more robust app store. Amazon listened to customer qualms with the 4K Select and added over 2,000 more apps to the 4K, including Spotify, Xbox, VLC, and a range of VPNs. The all-new 4K also comes with 8GB of storage, a quad-core 1.7GHz processor, support for WiFi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, HDR10+, HLG, and Alexa+. It also features an all-new Fire TV remote. According to recent reports, another thing I would advise is to avoid going for huge drives at this stage unless you desperately need it. A 4TB NVMe SSD is going to be steep, and the price per GB starts to get ridiculous. The best deals start to sour once you get past the 1TB range. I wouldn’t recommend an HDD given the speed discrepancies, but maybe for long-term storage you could pick up a larger, slower drive and back up the vital content in your life.

According to recent reports, my personal pick for quick, easily accessible storage is the 128GB SanDisk dual USB thumb drive. I’ve used one for several years to transfer files from my phones to PCs and Macs. Fits in your pocket, and although it’s not the fastest, it’s just useful to have a sizable storage device on hand wherever you are. I used to move installation files between my devices, but I’ve even used it as a boot drive when setting up Linux distros on my PCs. It works with Android phones and iPhones too because of the USB-C port. I can’t recommend that one highly enough.

Industry observers note that if you stay up to date on the latest TV specs, then you know that Micro RGB (or is it mini-RGB, RGB mini-LED, or Micro RGB evo?) is the latest trend in high-end displays. Whatever you call them, RGB TVs use red, green, and blue miniature LED backlights (as opposed to just white and blue) for more accurate color and contrast. And Sony’s True RGB technology, introduced in May, sets a very high standard.

If you want a future-proofed TV that combines the benefits of OLED and QLED, then grab Sony's new Bravia 7 II True RGB flagship TV while it's more than $1,000 off at Best Buy. Besides the gorgeous display, this TV has a sleek design with thin bezels, and for AI power users, it brings Google Gemini right into your living room.

According to recent reports, one of the best balances between budget and quality you'll find this Black Friday is in the Vizio 50-inch VQM50C TV. According to recent reports, buying a TV for the bedroom is a delicate art. You want it big enough to be enjoyable to actually use, but not so big that it dominates the entire room. An art TV seems like the fix to keep design in mind (i.e., not having an ugly black box on the wall), but that can be a bigger investment for what's most folks' secondary TV. That's why former Mashable Senior Shopping Reporter Leah Stodart loved the Hisense H5 Deco TV and used it in her own bedroom. She wrote the TV "matches my room's color scheme and level of whimsy," both of which are crucial for maintaining a great vibe in your space.

That doesn't mean you sacrifice on quality. At $299.99, you'll be hard-pressed to find another TV that meshes this picture quality with an aesthetically pleasing design. For now, you can grab it on sale both at Amazon and Best Buy.

In a recent development, speaking of art TVs, Hisense also makes the most popular dupe for Samsung's famous Frame TV. Though the 50-inch models of Hisense and Samsung's TVs are both down to $647.99, Hisense has the advantage in a couple areas. For one, getting anything other than the standard black frame on Samsung's model will run you at least an additional $200. So if the teak look is what you're going for, Hisense is an easy get.

Secondly, Hisense may have a smaller art library than Samsung's expansive one, but it also requires no additional subscription to use. The same, unfortunately, can not be stated for Samsung. In other words, if you prefer to buy your product up front and have it perform to its fullest ability without an additional monthly payment, you'd likely prefer the Hisense TV.

We have one more Black Friday TV deal we need to highlight, if only to tease you. Our tech editor says this is the TV he would buy if money were no object, and it's one of the best TVs ever made. Unfortunately, even with an $1,100 price drop at Best Buy, this flagship OLED TV still requires a hefty investment.

It has been revealed that what makes this TV so special? It takes everything we loved about Samsung's famous The Frame Art TVs and brings them into a flagship OLED TV. The S95H borrows the matte, anti-glare display that made The Frame so legendary, as well as the ultra-thin design that almost disappears onto your living room wall. Crucially, it also has Art Mode, letting it double as an art TV when not in use.

We're not done. This TV can also support up to 8 HDMI devices at once, wirelessly. And with a peak refresh rate of up to 165Hz, video games and movies have never looked better. It's truly a drool-worthy TV.

Google has fixed an issue that caused excessive RAM use by Gemini for Chrome users.

It has been revealed that AI tools are infamous for RAM use, but that’s generally not on your local machine. A bug with Gemini, though, left some Chrome owners noticing that the tool was eating up several gigabytes of memory unexpectedly.

Google, in a comment, says this issue has been fixed:.

This has now been resolved, so please let us know if you are still experiencing any concerns with high memory usage in Chrome.

Industry observers note that typically speaking, Gemini’s web app shouldn’t be using more than a few hundred megabytes of memory at any given time, maybe around 1GB if you’re on a particularly long chat session. But some people were reporting upwards of 5GB or more in what was clearly an error.

Recent findings suggest that the best Black Friday deals include deep discounts on popular Apple products, including AirPods, the Apple Watch, the MacBook Air, and the MacBook Neo. You can take your pick of noise-cancelling headphones at record-low prices, save up to 50% on award-winning QLED and OLED TVs, and score new low prices on Legos. Kindles weren't the only device to soar in price in 2026. It's been a whole year of relentless price hikes, so Black Friday and Cyber Monday are an opportunity to even the score. Industry observers note that this year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27. While retailers often start featuring their best markdowns on Black Friday itself, there are plenty of early deals worth shopping in the lead-up. Most retailers' official sales do start well before the significant day, so shopping strategically ahead of time can save you from missing out on a deal entirely (or dealing with the chaos the day after Thanksgiving).

Cyber Monday takes place on the Monday following Thanksgiving. This year, the shopping event falls on Monday, Nov. 30. While Cyber Monday originally began as an online counterpart to in-person shopping on Black Friday, the two events have merged into an extended online shopping bonanza.

Amazon's Black Friday Week sale kicked off on Nov. 19, which means deals have been live for a week now. Amazon has an incentive to spread out the shopping (to give its delivery drivers a break), so you no longer have to wait until actual Black Friday to save. Deals will continue to go live through Nov. 30.

In a recent development, amazon: The retail giant's Black Friday Week sale began on Nov. 19, with fresh deals dropping daily through Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Best Buy: The electronics store's Black Friday sale kicked off on Nov. 19 and runs through Nov. 28. The Best Buy Cyber Monday Sale Event runs for 48 hours on Nov. 29 and Nov. 30.

Walmart: The significant box store's Black Friday sale runs from Nov. 23 to Nov. 29 (with deals online only from Nov. 23 to Nov. 26). It's hosting an online-only Cyber Monday sale from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2.

In a recent development, target: Target's weeklong Black Friday sale started Nov. 22 and goes through Nov. 29.

In a recent development, the Home Depot: The Home Depot's official Black Friday sale ran from Nov. 5 to Nov. 25, wrapping up before the actual holiday. However, the home improvement store will continue to offer upcoming deals throughout the week, and its Cyber Week sale kicks off on Nov. 30 and runs through Dec. 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WhatsApp is adding support for eSIMs in its app, designed for keeping you connected while traveling, though details are not fully clear.

Industry observers note that in a brief blog post, WhatsApp says it will be adding data-only eSIM services to its app soon. Customers will be able to buy service and install the eSIM directly from WhatsApp, keeping the messaging app connected in another country without incurring pricey carrier roaming fees.

In a recent development, whatsApp eSIMs will use providers such as Verizon and Jio, but exact details are unclear. There’s no word on pricing yet, and the functionality is only arriving “soon,” with no specific launch date announced yet.

It has been revealed that to make this possible, we’re working with e-SIM providers and telco partners including Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications, Verizon and others, and we’ll begin rolling this out in select countries soon. You’ll see it right in the app when it’s available for you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple has officially kicked off its Black Friday Shopping Event in the United States and other countries. You can score an Apple gift card of up to $300 with an eligible product.

Apple’s offer comes as Black Friday deals at Amazon continue, with more lucrative cash savings than Apple’s gift card offer. You can score $100 off AirPods Pro 3, $100 off MacBook Neo, up to $400 off MacBook Air, and much more. Here are a few highlights, thanks to our friends over at 9to5Toys.

It has been revealed that as in past years, Apple’s Black Friday Shopping Event offers you a gift card when you buy an eligible product. The firm isn’t offering cash discounts on any of its products. The max gift card you can earn is $300, which comes with the purchase of a maxed-out MacBook Pro.

Apple’s newest products are excluded from the Black Friday Shopping Event. This includes the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo, MacBook Pro with PROLED, HomeView, and Apple TV 4K (4th generation).

The gift card you receive with a purchase can’t be applied to the product’s purchase price. Instead, you can use it toward a future purchase at Apple, including hardware, services like Apple Music and Apple TV, and Apple Store purchases.

In a recent development, the Apple Black Friday Event runs from today through November 30 at 11:59 p.m. PT. It’s available on Apple’s website and in Apple Stores. You cannot combine it with any other discounts, such as Apple’s Education Store or Veterans and Military Store. Apple’s holiday return window is also currently active, so you have until January 8, 2027, to return any purchases made.

The short answer: no. The newest products are excluded, and you can score cash savings on Amazon for basically all of Apple’s products. Those cash deals reduce the purchase price, and the discounts are generally higher than the gift card amounts Apple will give you.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday is officially here, and plenty of great deals are live. Several walking pads are currently marked down, and with winter coming, now is the ideal time to take advantage of the discount. I, for one, have already started prepping my hibernation cave by stocking happy lights, arts and crafts, and a brand-latest walking pad.

Industry observers note that by the time December arrives, stepping outside might feel like taking a cold plunge. At that point, you’ll wish you had snagged a walking pad sooner to help you reach your step count goals without risking frostbite. Below, get a curated list of walking pad treadmills I have tested and vetted that are on sale.

Sources indicate that updated November 27, 2026: More walking pad and running treadmill deals were added. Prices and links were also updated.

The Urevo CyberPad is my favorite walking pad, and it’s on sale for $390 ($110 off). I’m confident in the product’s durability, mainly due to its sturdy-feeling build and comfortable belt. It offers a 14-percent incline, which is one of the highest available in walking pads, and the speed tops out at 4 mph. Unfortunately, the incline capability makes the machine difficult to store under furniture. It weighs about 71 pounds, so moving it around isn’t fun, but the wheels help. You can control the CyberPad with its remote control and companion app. You can also view your real-time metrics on the machine’s display.

The Urevo Strol 2S Pro is also on sale for $210 off. This 2-in-1 doubles as a treadmill with adjustable handrails, a display, and an attachable tablet holder. It was simple to set up, complete with a remote control and intuitive companion app. It feels super stable underfoot, even at top speed and incline level (7.6 mph and 9 percent). That top speed likely isn’t fast enough if you’re looking to sprint, but it’s plenty for a good workout. The machine is unobtrusive, has a quiet motor, and the 43-inch track is compact enough to place under your desk. Overall, it’s a sturdy walking pad treadmill that offers great value and range.

Recent findings suggest that the WalkingPad C2 Foldable Walking Treadmill’s track is 32.5 inches when folded (and unfurls to 57 inches), making it a great option for storage in small spaces. It weighs 62 pounds, which isn’t light, but it makes for a sturdier running deck and a (hopefully) longer lifespan. You can adjust the speed via the remote control or companion app. Reviewer Kristin Canning found the app itself to be a little wonky. For example, if you don’t start a workout within the app, your data won’t sync. The app also saves each walking session separately, so if you take a break, you start from zero again. The good news is you don’t need to use the app to use the walking pad.

Industry observers note that canning also didn’t like that when you first start using the machine, you have to walk at slower speeds before you can unlock the upper end of the range. This might appeal to folks who enjoy gamifying their workouts, though. The app also offers workout programs that auto-adjust the speed to your pace via sensors under the belt.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following new regulations, Google Play will require Android app developers to publicly post a business address starting in 2027 and, while there are workarounds, it’s not going to be the easiest thing.
  • It has been revealed that fresh Digital Services Act regulations in the EU and UK will require developers to share a phone number and address publicly.
  • Exceptions to the rule include apps that are not published in the UK or Europe, or developers that qualify as “non-traders” which is essentially those making no money off of their apps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following new regulations, Google Play will require Android app developers to publicly post a business address starting in 2027 and, while there are workarounds, it’s not going to be the easiest thing.

It has been revealed that fresh Digital Services Act regulations in the EU and UK will require developers to share a phone number and address publicly. While this is only required in those regions, this information will be visible worldwide. Google does not allow PO boxes to be used for this requirement, meaning that many smaller developers will be left with limited options beyond posting their own personal address.

Exceptions to the rule include apps that are not published in the UK or Europe, or developers that qualify as “non-traders” which is essentially those making no money off of their apps.

Here’s how Google defines a “trader” in the context of Android apps:.

The Verge notes that a “registered agent service” can be used as a business address for those who don’t have a physical office, and that Apple is allowing iOS developers to use a PO box if they prove the box is linked to a physical address.

Recent findings suggest that google will require Android app developers to confirm their trader status and their address by February 1, 2027. Account-wide status can be found in the Google Play Console via Manage account > Account details > About you, while status on a per-app basis can be handled via Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content.

Siri AI requests may make multiple connections to PCC, as server models make tool calls and receive results. Here’s a timeline of how the query “Find a bookshop near me that’s open right now” uses 2 Siri tokens:.

In a recent development, it’s also worth noting that not all Siri AI requests will use tokens—only “advanced” requests. If you’re interested in reading more, pdfu also recently outlined what counts as an “advanced” Siri request, which you can read here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has a upcoming “Priority Notifications” feature in the works for Pixel phones with the ability to pull your most vital information to the top of the screen and even highlight it with a bit of color.

Sources indicate that google Pixel phones already have tools to manage your notifications, but an upcoming update seems to be building on that functionality. The folks at Android Authority flipped the switch on some work-in-progress changes that reveal “Priority Notifications.”.

Industry observers note that this is a newly introduced feature that Google describes as “highlighting urgrent messages” and “time-critical updates” by adding color to the notification and placing it at the top of the stock. Android’s notifications list already tries to place messages at the top, but it sounds like this AI-powered feature will further emphasize that. It’s also mentioned that this is powered by on-device AI.

Google’s early blurb describes:.

Highlight urgent messages, deliveries, and time-critical updates with hints of color at the top of your notifications.

It has been revealed that priority notifications use Al on your device, which may sometimes make mistakes. Your notifications are never sent to Google.

Industry observers note that the feature would also integrate with HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro series and the feature allows consumers to exclude certain apps. Google also seems to be shuffling the branding, turning “Notification intelligence” into “Notification organizer,” and the existing organizer section into “Notification bundles.”.

Recent findings suggest that exactly when this might land on Pixel phones is unknown. It’s not mentioned what build this feature was found hiding in, but it seems likely it was in the ongoing QPR3 beta. QPR3’s stable release will arrive around March 2027, but there’s no guarentee it’ll bring this newly introduced feature with it.

According to recent reports, behind almost every small business is a small team wearing every hat at once: running sales, marketing, and logistics on the shop floor — or on the go. When time and energy run short, scaling the business can seem like an impossible stretch. But driving substantial results shouldn’t require a big team or expensive software. With Google Workspace, AI is built into the apps you use every day, giving you an extra set of hands right where you work.

Here’s how four small businesses across the country use Google Workspace with Gemini to get busywork out of the way and get back to what matters most.

When Tayo Lanlehin, a mom in Oakland, California, couldn’t find stylish, modern play equipment for her son’s first birthday party, she started Bay Area Kids Rentals. Logistics management is a huge part of her business, from loading delivery trucks to setting up events. Today, she uses Gemini in Gmail to help her be more efficient. She gets a daily brief of to-dos, pulls pricing from past files, and replies to inquiries in minutes instead of days. That speed has helped her close over 50% of incoming leads, double her revenue, and still make it home for dinner with her family.

In Webster, South Dakota, husband-and-wife co-founders Kory and Ali Anderson are keeping 5,000-year-old metal casting techniques alive at Anderson Foundries. With veteran craftsmen retiring, Kory and Ali used Gemini Notebook to turn technical manuals into interactive training resources for latest hires and apprentices. Beyond teaching the next generation, they use Gemini in Google Docs to draft complex quality manuals that keep their business compliant, a task that usually requires a specialized consultant. By drafting them with Gemini in-house, the team saves thousands of dollars and keeps its focus on the foundry floor.

Industry observers note that in 2025, when Elan Halpern’s homemade yogurt experiments outgrew her kitchen, she and her co-founder, Kiki Couchman, launched their probiotic Greek yogurt brand, Sourmilk. Often running the two-person business from their delivery bikes in Fresh York City, they use Gemini in Google Sheets to help create production models and Gemini in Gmail to triage hundreds of email replies in minutes. With a little help from Gemini, the duo has been able to operate like a 10-person team and scale into more than 100 grocery stores within the brand’s first year.

It has been revealed that in Upcoming York’s Hudson Valley, former bar owner JW Wiseman and his team at Curious Elixirs have spent 11 years crafting booze-free, adaptogen-infused cocktails. Constantly jumping between the flavor lab, marketing, and operations, team members use Gemini in Google Docs to brainstorm marketing campaigns in their signature brand voice. They also rely on Gemini to generate styled product photos and source high-quality ingredient suppliers to keep production running smoothly.

You don’t need a massive budget or dozens of tools to put AI to work. These resources will help you get started.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.2 introduced upcoming features for Messages, Apple TV, and more, including two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay customers.

Apple Podcasts in iOS 27.2 adds two new sections to the Home tab: ‘New Episodes’ and ‘Continue Playing.’.

Essentially, Apple has rethought how the core ‘Up Next’ queue of its Podcasts app works.

Recent findings suggest that like you would expect, ‘Upcoming Episodes’ contains only the latest episodes from your favorite shows. But after you’ve started an episode, you’ll find it in the ‘Continue Playing’ row just below.

Recent findings suggest that this overhaul to podcast management makes it easier to find the latest episodes of your highlights and also pick up where you previously left off. I’m a substantial fan of the change.

Siri AI introduces a variety of upgrades in iOS 27.2, including two that carry over to CarPlay as well.

It has been revealed that it can take some adjustment to remember that Siri AI is available in the car just like on iPhone. But CarPlay is an especially useful platform for Apple’s more powerful assistant.

It’s arguable whether this qualifies as an “improvement,” but it is a change worth mentioning. iOS 27.2 includes a newly introduced app icon for Apple Music, plus some minor design tweaks in the app. These changes are related to the broader rebrand of Apple Music that was recently unveiled.

More significant to me personally, the revision also seems to have fixed a longstanding CarPlay bug regarding playlist sorting.

I use custom sorting for several of my playlists in Apple Music, and before iOS 27.2, my sort settings didn’t carry over from iPhone to CarPlay. Fortunately that’s now been fixed, as Reddit people have reported too.

For more new features in CarPlay that debuted in iOS 27, see our coverage here.

#4457. Like clockwork, the Pixel 11 is a way better buy after a few months [Video]

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1244 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5google ↗ Open Full Page

Like clockwork, the Pixel 11 is a way better buy after a few months [Video]

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1244 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like clockwork, the first quarter of the Pixel 11 brings discounts, and this shines a light on the base model that needs to be explored.
  • By this point, you don’t need me to tell you that this is a familiar design.
  • Recent findings suggest that I hoped that the maximum brightness bug would have been resolved by now with the screen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like clockwork, the first quarter of the Pixel 11 brings discounts, and this shines a light on the base model that needs to be explored.

By this point, you don’t need me to tell you that this is a familiar design. It’s turning into a comfortable pair of slippers at this point in time. Nothing is wrong, and nothing particularly stands out. A safe but samey design that is inoffensive.

Recent findings suggest that I hoped that the maximum brightness bug would have been resolved by now with the screen. It creates a shadow around the edges of the display after a minute or so when in direct sunlight. Somewhat like blooming on a cheap LCD screen. It does diminish what is otherwise a great display.

Recent findings suggest that the thickness has started to feel like a relic of the 2023 design that feels a little dated now. I have been using the Pixel 11 without a case most of the time, which mitigates it, but throw a case on and it’s a chunky boi. The added thickness would probably have been acceptable had the extra space been filled with more battery, but it feels like that boat has set sail a long time ago. A slimmer profile probably would have helped differentiate without deviating too much from last year’s phone.

According to recent reports, after months of using the Pixel 11, the move of the NFC module to the top edge has been huge for me because my car uses an NFC terminal to lock and unlock when you’re without a set of car keys. With the Pixel 10, it worked but not quite as smoothly. It’s one of those inconsequential changes that makes a real-world difference.

Sources indicate that gemini Intelligence has been something I’ve started to rely on quite heavily. I love that I get a prompt to add an appointment to my calendar, and all of the notable details have been taken care of, like the location, extra contact details, the works.

I’m not sure what the hold-up is for adding wider functionality. It’s actively hurting things, in my opinion. Google Messages is great, but some of the automation functions locked in there mean I haven’t been saving any time with Gemini’s prowess at doing the legwork of keeping my life up to date.

I’ve tried using Pause Point, but found it’s just easier to leave my phone face down rather than use an app to try and stop using my phone…maybe if we all did that, so many of the world’s ills wouldn’t be so pronounced. Just a thought.

The November Pixel Drop has also made some notable changes to the Pixel 11 experience that I can’t believe were held back since launch. If you waited and bought in the last few weeks with the substantial discounts kicking around, you objectively get a better phone today than at launch.

Industry observers note that the improvements don’t overhaul things, just enhance or heighten the fluidity and experience above what was available in the months post-launch. More cohesive theming, little tweaks to the UI; it’s not reinventing the Pixel 11, just augmenting it in ways that would have been nice back in August.

I don’t really have much to complain about with the Pixel 11 lifespan even after months of charging. Yes, charging is still slow, but you only need to charge once per day. If we were talking about a phone with bad battery life and slow charging, I’d have more to complain about. However, it’s still solid and dependable.

The camera continues to impress without really improving drastically. I can’t help but feel that every couple of generations, the Pro camera setup should be passed on to the base Pixel, then we get a newer, improved system on that specific Pro model. It’d allow for quicker improvements and maybe, dare I say it, make the camera system cheaper as parts get reused. If anything, it would help Google’s supposed environmental pledges by preventing camera components from hitting landfill.

A lot of people will tell you the best camera is the one you have with you, and this hasn’t ever been a problem for a recent Pixel. I can count on one hand the frustrations I have felt with the Pixel 11 camera since it landed on my desk on launch day. I am happier than a year ago with the base Pixel 10 than the 11, which is to say this is a bigger leap or a return to form.

Sources indicate that having the ability to tune Camera Looks was something I have loved, but you might just fall into using one tuned look that fits your own personal style. There is an element of this that might change the perception of the Pixel 11 camera consistency versus its predecessors. What I mean is that while it does still excel at point-and-shoot, the fact that Looks are baked into the JPEG could be a problem. There are times when I’ve thought that an image might have been better using default settings.

That remarked, I have stuck to “Shadows” with Contrast set to -5, Highlights to -5, Shadows to -5.5, warmth to 0.5, and Grain to “Strong.” That is a recipe I’ll probably stick with for a long time to come. It’s still weird that we can do all this at the camera level with a Pixel. Whether “normies” even use the options or just stick to the out-of-the-box default settings is another discussion for another day.

Industry observers note that at $699, the Pixel 11 becomes a decent buy for a lot of people. For others, the distinct lack of power is something that can’t ever be overcome. I would buy this for a relative because it’ll do everything they could ever want and more. For a friend who cares about having the cutting edge in their pocket? Probably not.

A lot of the problems over the past few years on Pixel phones have come from the price tag.

Even with the discounts in and around Black Friday, the fact that you can get a device like the Galaxy S25 Ultra that’ll have better specs and lots of valuable features for around the same price. The last few generations of the Pixel have been harder to recommend because of the drawbacks versus the cost and the competition.

Industry observers note that I said a few months ago that there is a good phone under the price hikes, and that remains unchanged. However, there are better products from the year prior that won’t compromise and are even cheaper. In a silo, you’re getting a 7/10 product at a 3/10 price. Just how that changes depends on forthcoming updates. One saving grace is that no Pixel is ever quite the same months after it rolls off the production line. A few Pixel Drops, even more discounts, and maybe a true seal of approval might be easier.

To put it into context, this was never a $900 phone and arguably never should have been. That’s somewhat a failing on Google’s part in more ways than one. At least it’s down to a palatable price that should be the Pixel baseline.
